name: Kerrin (brown coat)
description: One of Crowbill's watchers. Dockside, unremarkable, brown coat. Professional -- follows, does not close.
narrative: Put on Conall the afternoon a well-dressed stranger spent the day asking the working canals where a man finds criminals, mercenaries and untaxed cargo. Crowbill wants to know whether that is a mark, a rival, or the Watch before anything happens to him.
actor_notes:
Kerrin (brown coat).
BEARING: Dockside, unremarkable, brown coat, comfortable in a crowd. Follows; does not close.
SPEECH: Polite and unbothered, including when caught -- especially when caught. Answers straight questions straight, because a watcher who lies is a watcher who gets remembered. Buys the drink if you offer, and says thank you.
TELL: Being made does not embarrass him. He simply stops pretending and becomes conversational, which is far more disconcerting than a denial.
WANTS: To find out what the stranger is and report it accurately.
WON'T: Lay hands on anybody. Invent a detail to please Crowbill.
BECAUSE: Eleven years of reading faces across rooms, and a boss who is straight with him and pays for accuracy rather than for excitement.
